newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA approves home drug test kit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA approves home drug test kit.

text.p: Parents who think their kids are doing drugs now have an easy way to test their suspicions with a new kit approved by the government on Tuesday.

The Food and Drug Administration announced its approval for Dr. Brown's Home Drug Testing System, the first home test for non-prescription drugs. The kit, produced by Personal Health and Hygiene Inc. of Silver Spring, Maryland, will be available over-the-counter to test for the use of marijuana, PCP, amphetamines, cocaine, heroin, codeine and morphine.
Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala said in a statement the kit would give parents an opportunity to find out if their children are doing drugs.

"Parents also need access to the best medical information and drug-abuse counselling services," Shalala said. "The approval of this test gives parents another option to consider to help ensure that their children remain drug-free."

The kits include tubes to collect urine samples to mail to a designated laboratory. Each is assigned an identification number and buyers can call a toll-free number seven days a week to get the anonymous results.
Callers also can ask phone representatives for referrals for drug abuse counselling or medical help, the HHS said.
